docs.title: Documentation
docs.text:
Setup and operations guides for the Traefik infrastructure stack.

Guide Description Getting Started Prerequisites, environment variables, startup order DNS & Domains Cloudflare DNS for all platform zones TLS & Certificates Origin certificates and Let's Encrypt fallback Monitoring Prometheus, Grafana, Loki, and Promtail Sentry Cloud Hosted error tracking (recommended for 12 GB RAM) Self-Hosted Sentry On-prem Sentry via official installer (16 GB+ RAM) Routing & ADMS Docker labels, middlewares, biometric device HTTP Troubleshooting Common issues and fixes

docs.title: DNS & Domains
docs.text: All zones are expected to be proxied through Cloudflare with SSL/TLS mode: Full (strict).

docs.title: musfiqdehan.com
docs.text:
Apex only — no *.musfiqdehan.com tenant wildcard.

Record Target musfiqdehan.com Server IP (A/AAAA)

Add explicit hostnames as needed (e.g. grafana.musfiqdehan.com).

docs.title: Tenant platform domains (wildcard)
docs.text:
Wildcard DNS does not cover the apex. For each UK zone, create both apex and wildcard records:

Zone Apex Wildcard mrdfit.uk mrdfit.uk → server *.mrdfit.uk → server mrderp.uk mrderp.uk → server *.mrderp.uk → server mrdhrms.uk mrdhrms.uk → server *.mrdhrms.uk → server mrdlms.uk mrdlms.uk → server *.mrdlms.uk → server

Proxy both records (orange cloud) to the same origin.

docs.title: Stale records
docs.text: Remove any old A/AAAA/CNAME records pointing to Hostinger parking, a previous VPS, or another host. Mixed records cause intermittent routing to the wrong origin.

docs.title: HTTP redirect rules
docs.text:
Port-80 → HTTPS redirects for /api, /ninja, /media, /static, and /ws are defined in dynamic/redirects.yml:

  • Platform hosts: musfiqdehan.com (apex), plus apex + *. for each UK zone above
  • Custom domains: all other hostnames (tenant-owned domains)

ADMS device paths (/iclock, /cdata, etc.) stay on plain HTTP — see Routing & ADMS.

docs.title: Cloudflare API token
docs.text:
For Let's Encrypt DNS-01, create a token with Zone → DNS → Edit and Zone → Zone → Read scoped to every zone:

musfiqdehan.com, mrdfit.uk, mrderp.uk, mrdhrms.uk, mrdlms.uk

Set as CF_DNS_API_TOKEN in .env.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• Docker and Docker Compose
  • Domains managed in Cloudflare
  • Origin certificates and/or a Cloudflare API token for Let's Encrypt DNS-01
  • Application stacks (Django, Next.js, etc.) configured to join the traefik_proxy network

docs.title: Environment variables
docs.text:
Copy the example file and fill in secrets:

cp .env.example .env
Variable Used by Purpose CF_DNS_API_TOKEN Traefik Let's Encrypt DNS-01 for all managed zones GRAFANA_ADMIN_USER Grafana Admin username (default admin) GRAFANA_ADMIN_PASSWORD Grafana Admin password for Grafana UI

See .env.example for details.

docs.title: Grafana edge basic auth
docs.text:
Before starting the monitoring stack:

htpasswd -cb dynamic/.htpasswd admin 'your-strong-password'

This file is gitignored. See dynamic/.htpasswd.example.

docs.title: Startup order
docs.text:
# 1. Traefik — creates traefik_proxy network
docker compose --env-file .env -f docker-compose.traefik.yml up -d

# 2. Monitoring — metrics and logs
docker compose --env-file .env -f docker-compose.monitoring.yml up -d

# 3. Application stacks (from their respective repositories)
# docker compose -f <app>/docker-compose.prod.yml up -d --build

Traefik must start first so traefik_proxy exists for app and monitoring containers.

docs.text:

docs.title: Monitoring Stack
docs.text: Docker-based observability: Prometheus (metrics), Grafana (dashboards), Loki + Promtail (container logs).

docs.title: Components
docs.text:
Service Image role Exposure Prometheus Metrics store (15-day retention) Internal only Grafana UI at https://grafana.musfiqdehan.com Via Traefik + basic auth Loki Log store (14-day retention) Internal only Promtail Ships all Docker json-file logs to Loki Internal only node-exporter Host CPU, RAM, disk, network Internal only cAdvisor Per-container resource usage Internal only

Config lives under monitoring/. Compose file: docker-compose.monitoring.yml.

On a 12 GB RAM server, this stack plus Traefik and application containers is reasonable.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
1. Traefik running (traefik_proxy network exists)
  2. dynamic/.htpasswd created — see Getting Started
  3. GRAFANA_ADMIN_PASSWORD set in .env

docs.title: Start
docs.text: docker compose --env-file .env -f docker-compose.monitoring.yml up -d

docs.title: Grafana access
docs.text:
Layer Credentials Traefik edge dynamic/.htpasswd (htpasswd user/password) Grafana app GRAFANA_ADMIN_USER / GRAFANA_ADMIN_PASSWORD from .env

URL: https://grafana.musfiqdehan.com

Prometheus and Loki datasources are auto-provisioned from monitoring/grafana/provisioning/.

docs.title: Recommended dashboards
docs.text:
Import by ID in Grafana → Dashboards → Import:

ID Name 1860 Node Exporter Full 193 Docker cAdvisor 11462 Traefik 2.x (compatible with Traefik 3 metrics)

docs.title: Log queries (Explore → Loki)
docs.text:
{container_name=~".+"}
{compose_service="backend"}
{container_name=~".*postgres.*|.*redis.*"}

Promtail reads /var/lib/docker/containers and the Docker socket — all containers on the host that use the default json-file log driver are included.

docs.title: Verification
docs.text:
docker run --rm --network traefik_proxy curlimages/curl:latest \
  -s http://prometheus:9090/-/healthy

docker run --rm --network traefik_proxy curlimages/curl:latest \
  -s http://traefik:8080/metrics | head

Traefik exposes Prometheus metrics on internal entrypoint :8080 — see traefik.yml.

docs.title: Security
docs.text:
• Do not publish Prometheus, Loki, or cAdvisor ports on the host
  • Do not add Traefik labels to internal monitoring services except Grafana

docs.title: How Traefik discovers services
docs.text:
Containers must:

  • Join the traefik_proxy network
  • Set traefik.enable=true
  • Define router rules (Host(...), HostRegexp(...))
  • Point to the correct backend port
  • Optionally set tls.certresolver=letsencrypt with explicit tls.domains

Example labels:

labels:
  - traefik.enable=true
  - traefik.http.routers.api.rule=Host(`api.musfiqdehan.com`)
  - traefik.http.routers.api.entrypoints=websecure
  - traefik.http.routers.api.tls=true
  - traefik.http.routers.api.tls.certresolver=letsencrypt
  - traefik.http.services.api.loadbalancer.server.port=8000
  - traefik.http.routers.api.middlewares=security-headers@file,compress@file

For UK tenant subdomains, use HostRegexp in application compose files, e.g. ^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]*\.mrdfit\.uk$.

docs.title: Middlewares
docs.text:
Defined in dynamic/middlewares.yml. Reference as <name>@file in labels.

Middleware Purpose security-headers@file HSTS, XSS protection, X-Forwarded-Proto: https adms-http-headers@file Plain HTTP for devices — no HSTS, X-Forwarded-Proto: http compress@file Response compression api-ratelimit@file 100 req/s average, burst 50 ws-headers@file WebSocket upgrade passthrough redirect-to-https@file HTTP → HTTPS scheme redirect monitoring-basic-auth@file Basic auth for Grafana edge

docs.title: ADMS device routing (HTTP-only)
docs.text:
ZKTeco iClock biometric devices poll over plain HTTP on port 80. Browsers and APIs use HTTPS on port 443.

Device  → http://{host}/iclock/cdata?SN=...  → Traefik :80 → Daphne :8021
Browser → https://{host}/api/v1/...          → Traefik :443 (rate limited)

docs.title: Router split (backend labels)
docs.text:
Router Entrypoint Paths Rate limit backend-api websecure (443) /api, /ninja, /media, /static Yes backend-ws websecure (443) /ws No backend-adms web (80) /iclock, /cdata, /getrequest, /devicecmd No backend-custom-* same pattern custom tenant domains same

HTTPS ADMS paths are intentionally not routed.

docs.title: Device URL format
docs.text:
http://{tenant}.mrdfit.uk/iclock
http://{tenant}.mrderp.uk/iclock
http://musfiqdehan.com/iclock
http://{custom-domain}/iclock

Supported endpoints:

  • /iclock/cdata or /cdata — heartbeat + attendance
  • /iclock/getrequest or /getrequest — command poll
  • /iclock/devicecmd or /devicecmd — command acknowledgement

docs.title: Smoke test
docs.text:
curl -v "http://tenant.mrdfit.uk/iclock/cdata?SN=YOUR_SN"    # must succeed
curl -v "https://tenant.mrdfit.uk/iclock/cdata?SN=YOUR_SN"   # must not reach ADMS

docs.title: Cloudflare
docs.text: If domains are proxied, ensure port 80 reaches the origin for device hostnames (grey-cloud device subdomains, or rules allowing HTTP on /iclock/*).

docs.title: Port 80 selective redirect
docs.text: dynamic/redirects.yml redirects /api, /ninja, /media, /static, and /ws to HTTPS on platform hosts while leaving ADMS paths on HTTP.

docs.title: Sentry Cloud
docs.text:
Recommended for servers with limited RAM (e.g. 12 GB). No containers run on this host for Sentry.

Sentry captures application errors (exceptions, stack traces, releases). It does not replace Loki for raw container logs — use Monitoring for log aggregation.

docs.title: Setup
docs.text:
1. Create an account at sentry.io
  2. Create an organization
  3. Create one project per application (Django API, Next.js frontend, NestJS API, etc.)
  4. Copy each project's DSN from Settings → Projects → [project] → Client Keys (DSN)

No Traefik routes or DNS records are required — apps send events outbound to Sentry's ingest endpoints.

docs.title: SDK wiring
docs.text:
App Package Environment variable Django backend sentry-sdk[django] SENTRY_DSN, SENTRY_ENVIRONMENT Next.js frontend @sentry/nextjs NEXT_PUBLIC_SENTRY_DSN NestJS API @sentry/nestjs SENTRY_DSN

DSN format:

https://<key>@o<org-id>.ingest.<region>.sentry.io/<project-id>

docs.title: Django example
docs.text:
import os
import sentry_sdk

sentry_sdk.init(
    dsn=os.environ["SENTRY_DSN"],
    environment=os.environ.get("SENTRY_ENVIRONMENT", "production"),
    traces_sample_rate=0.1,
)

docs.title: When to use self-hosted instead
docs.text: See Self-Hosted Sentry if you have 16 GB+ RAM (24 GB+ with monitoring) and need data residency or air-gapped deployment.

docs.title: Self-Hosted Sentry
docs.text:
Run Sentry on your own infrastructure using the official self-hosted installer.

Resource requirements: 16 GB RAM minimum for Sentry alone; 24 GB+ recommended if Prometheus/Grafana/Loki run on the same host. On a 12 GB VPS, use Sentry Cloud instead.

Sentry is not a single Docker image — the installer deploys Postgres, Redis, Kafka, ClickHouse, Snuba, Relay, web, workers, cron, and more.

docs.title: Install
docs.text:
# Sibling directory to this repo, e.g. ~/DevOps/sentry-self-hosted
git clone https://github.com/getsentry/self-hosted.git
cd self-hosted
./install.sh

Follow the interactive installer to create an admin user and generate docker-compose.yml.

Keep Sentry in its own directory — do not merge into docker-compose.monitoring.yml. Upgrades use Sentry's ./install.sh.

docs.title: Expose via Traefik
docs.text: After installation, configure the public URL and attach to the existing proxy network.

docs.title: 1. Set URL prefix
docs.text:
Edit sentry/config.yml:

system.url-prefix: 'https://sentry.musfiqdehan.com'

docs.title: 2. Attach web service to traefik_proxy
docs.text:
In Sentry's docker-compose.yml, on the web service:

services:
  web:
    networks:
      - default
      - traefik_proxy
    labels:
      - traefik.enable=true
      - traefik.http.routers.sentry.rule=Host(`sentry.musfiqdehan.com`)
      - traefik.http.routers.sentry.entrypoints=websecure
      - traefik.http.routers.sentry.tls=true
      - traefik.http.services.sentry.loadbalancer.server.port=9000

networks:
  traefik_proxy:
    external: true

Ensure Traefik is running and sentry.musfiqdehan.com DNS points to the server.

docs.title: 3. Create admin user
docs.text:
During ./install.sh or afterward:

docker compose exec web sentry createuser

Disable public signup in Sentry admin after setup.

docs.title: Application SDK wiring
docs.text:
Create one Sentry project per app in the self-hosted UI. DSN format:

https://<key>@sentry.musfiqdehan.com/<project-id>
App Package Env var Django backend sentry-sdk[django] SENTRY_DSN Next.js frontend @sentry/nextjs NEXT_PUBLIC_SENTRY_DSN NestJS API @sentry/nestjs SENTRY_DSN

docs.title: Startup order (with Traefik + monitoring)
docs.text:
# 1. Traefik
docker compose --env-file .env -f docker-compose.traefik.yml up -d

# 2. Monitoring
docker compose --env-file .env -f docker-compose.monitoring.yml up -d

# 3. Sentry (from sentry-self-hosted directory)
docker compose up -d

docs.title: Upgrades
docs.text: Follow the official upgrade guide. Always run ./install.sh from the self-hosted repo after pulling a new release tag.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: Issue Check Web UI 502 docker compose ps — wait for Kafka/ClickHouse health Events not ingested Relay and worker containers running; DSN matches system.url-prefix OOM kills dmesg / docker stats — add RAM or move Sentry to a dedicated host CSRF errors system.url-prefix must match the browser URL exactly (https, no trailing slash)

docs.title: TLS & Certificates
docs.text:
Traefik supports two certificate sources:

  1. Cloudflare Origin Certificates (primary) — long-lived, loaded from certs/
  2. Let's Encrypt (fallback) — DNS-01 via Cloudflare API, configured in traefik.yml

docs.title: musfiqdehan.com
docs.text:
Default cert files:

  • certs/origin.pem — public certificate
  • certs/origin.key — private key

Loaded by dynamic/tls.yml as the default certificate.

docs.title: UK platform zones
docs.text:
Create a separate origin certificate per zone in Cloudflare (SSL/TLS → Origin Server):

Zone Certificate hostnames mrdfit.uk mrdfit.uk, *.mrdfit.uk mrderp.uk mrderp.uk, *.mrderp.uk mrdhrms.uk mrdhrms.uk, *.mrdhrms.uk mrdlms.uk mrdlms.uk, *.mrdlms.uk

Save as e.g. certs/mrdfit.pem / certs/mrdfit.key and add matching blocks in dynamic/tls.yml.

Never commit certificate or key files to git.

docs.title: Create an origin certificate
docs.text:
1. Cloudflare Dashboard → SSL/TLS → Origin Server
  2. Create Certificate → select hostnames for the zone
  3. Save PEM and key into certs/

docs.title: Let's Encrypt fallback
docs.text:
Wildcard certs require DNS-01. The letsencrypt resolver in traefik.yml uses provider: cloudflare and reads CF_DNS_API_TOKEN.

Production app routers should declare explicit domains on labels:

- traefik.http.routers.api.tls.certresolver=letsencrypt
- traefik.http.routers.api.tls.domains[0].main=mrdfit.uk
- traefik.http.routers.api.tls.domains[0].sans=*.mrdfit.uk

Traefik cannot infer ACME domains from a regex-only HostRegexp rule.

ACME state is stored in the Docker volume traefik_letsencrypt at /letsencrypt inside the Traefik container.

docs.title: Certificate selection flow
docs.text:
HTTPS request → origin cert in tls.yml matches SNI?
  Yes → serve origin cert
  No  → router has certresolver=letsencrypt?
          Yes → request/use LE cert for tls.domains
          No  → default cert or TLS error

docs.title: TLS & certificates
docs.text: Symptom Fix Browser certificate warning Confirm certs/origin.pem and origin.key exist and match Cloudflare; or set CF_DNS_API_TOKEN for LE fallback UK apex works, subdomains don't Add wildcard DNS *.zone.uk — wildcard does not cover apex and vice versa Let's Encrypt fails Check Traefik logs for ACME errors; verify Cloudflare token has DNS Edit on the zone Wrong cert served Add per-zone cert block in dynamic/tls.yml or explicit tls.domains on router

docs.title: Routing
docs.text: Symptom Fix Service unreachable Container on traefik_proxy? traefik.enable=true? 404 from Traefik Router rule / host mismatch; check labels Wrong scheme in Django Requests must pass Cloudflare → Traefik; trusted IPs in traefik.yml Stale Hostinger page Remove conflicting DNS records for the hostname

docs.title: Monitoring
docs.text: Symptom Fix Grafana 401 at edge Create dynamic/.htpasswd via htpasswd No logs in Loki Promtail needs /var/lib/docker/containers + docker.sock mounts Traefik target DOWN in Prometheus Restart Traefik after enabling metrics.prometheus; scrape traefik:8080

docs.title: ADMS devices
docs.text: Symptom Fix Device cannot connect Use http:// not https://; port 80 open through Cloudflare 404 on /iclock backend-adms router must use web entrypoint (port 80)

docs.title: Useful commands
docs.text:
# Traefik logs
docker logs traefik --tail 100

# Reload dynamic config (file provider watches automatically)
docker exec traefik ls /etc/traefik/dynamic/

# List routers (if dashboard enabled temporarily)
docker logs traefik 2>&1 | grep -i error
